newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere B shares up in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere B shares up in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere B shares hit a new 16-month high on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Friday, rising to $12.25 from $12.
But Solidere A shares fell back to $11.5 on profit-taking after touching $11.75 on Thursday.
Dealers said holders of A shares, distributed to former property owners in the Beirut city centre in exchange for their rights, rushed to sell at their highest level in more than a year.

"The high demand for B shares reflects continued interest by longterm investors in these shares before the dividend declaration on May 27, while owners of the A shares rushed to sell at a high price," broker Carole Deeb of Credit Commercial et Foncier told Reuters.
The fall of the A shares dragged the LISPI and BLOM general indices down 0.31 percent and 0.51 percent to 88.37 and 1,008 respectively.
The LIBX bank index was unchanged at 139.75 as the three listed banks held steady in active trade.
Bank of Beirut was at $3.5625, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce at $17.25 and Banque Audi $20.125.
Total market turnover was 335,408 shares for a value of $4,522,119 from 376,828 shares and $3,631,208 on Wednesday.
Among the four industrial companies only 450 shares of pipemaker Eternit changed hands, down at $1.875 from $1.9375. There was no trade in Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
